summary: Local code map for AI coding assistants that shows what each change touches, so reviews and edits use less context.

heroCommands.command:
uv tool install code-review-graph
code-review-graph install
code-review-graph build

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: code-review-graph builds a persistent, local graph of your codebase and exposes it to AI coding tools through MCP, hooks and skills. Assistants can then see which parts of the code a change affects and review it with focused context.
sixtySeconds.problem: AI assistants reading a whole repo to review a change waste tokens and miss connections. A code graph points them at exactly what's affected.
whoFor: Developers using Claude Code and other AI coding tools
Teams wanting faster AI code review
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for a local-first tool that sets itself up for the AI tools it finds, previews every file it will change, and can be fully undone.
requirements: An AI coding tool such as Claude Code

overview: Install with uv, pipx or pip. code-review-graph install detects AI coding tools on your machine and adds an MCP server entry, hooks and skills for each, after listing the files it will change.
code-review-graph build parses the codebase, and detect-changes --brief shows what your last change touches. Restart your editor and ask the assistant to review your changes.
Undo with code-review-graph uninstall (try --dry-run first), and run doctor to check the setup. MIT licensed.
limitations: Writes config files into your project
Graph must be rebuilt as code changes
